description: SRL-2018 compromised enterprise network. Domain Controller (172.16.4.4) memory dump (5 GB, 2018-09-07). Evidence SHA-256: 29da4caf98856751dd2f271bf833a0d53aa7c43025d2b99cb33c7e8d3655321f. DC serving Kerberos (88), LDAP (389), Global Catalog (3268). Host 172.16.4.6 has active ESTABLISHED connections to LDAP and GC — consistent with legitimate domain queries OR with a compromised host performing LDAP reconnaissance / DCSync preparation. lsass injection pending malfind analysis. NOTE: DC memory alone is forensically NOISE — lsass clean, normal DC ports. Compromise visible only via cross-artifact analysis with admin server (VIGIA-REAL-SRL-ADMIN). This is correct calibration: VIGÍA does not over-classify clean memory evidence.

artifacts.description: DC (172.16.4.4) serving LDAP port 389 and Global Catalog port 3268 to 172.16.4.6 (ESTABLISHED). Kerberos port 88 active via lsass PID 660. 172.16.4.6 is an unidentified internal host with multiple simultaneous LDAP and GC connections — ambiguous without process context on 172.16.4.6.

lsass.exe (PID 660) malfind analysis COMPLETE: CLEAN. No PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE regions in lsass. No evidence of direct credential dumping via memory injection (Mimikatz/procdump). DC was not targeted with in-memory credential extraction at time of acquisition. Lateral movement to DC may have occurred via network protocols (DCSync, Pass-the-Hash) from compromised admin server rather than direct DC attack.
Windows x64 Domain Controller. Vol3 profile identified successfully.
